page.overview:
What is Dor Dínen?

Dor Dhínen, the Silent Land, was a small, roughly triangular, deserted part of East Beleriand, north of Doriath.

Contained by one of the upper courses of the Esgalduin (bordering Nan Dungortheb) and the Aros (bordering Himlad), it was said that no one had lived there for ages. The region was crossed by a road passing from the Iant Iaur on the Esgalduin to the Arossiach on the Aros that led to the northern marches of Himlad. The southern edge of Dor Dhínen bordered the Forest of Neldoreth and the Forest of Region while the northern edge bordered Ered Gorgoroth. The region was best known for the Arossiach, which connected the Esgalduin and Aros.

Dor Dhínen was a Sindarin name meaning "silent land" consisting of the words dôr ("dwelling-place, region where certain people live; land") and d(h)ínen from the elements dîn ("silence; quiet") and -en
